chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the performance of voluntary prayer while resident, mounted on an animal, when I was leaving near the dwellings of Kufa, or if I was in a hurry in Kufa. He said: 'If you are in a hurry and cannot dismount, fearing the loss of the prayer time if you leave it while mounted, then yes (it is permissible); otherwise, your prayer on the ground is more beloved to me.'

key_terms.عَلَى ظَهْرِ الدَّابَّةِ: On the back of the animal

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to pray voluntary prayers while mounted on an animal during residence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in performing voluntary prayers while mounted during residence (al-Hadar), prioritizing the preservation of prayer time over the ideal posture. It establishes a hierarchy of preference where praying on the ground is superior unless urgency (hurrying) creates a risk of missing the prayer window, reflecting the Shia principle of balancing ease with reverence. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for understanding the conditions under which the 'prayer of the traveler' or 'prayer while mounted' concessions apply even within city limits.
